newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - S.African rand seen at 4.77 in Q4 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - S.African rand seen at 4.77 in Q4 1997.

text.p: The South African rand is expected to continue to depreciate over the next 15 months albeit at a slower pace than the 25 percent slide seen over the last seven months.

According to the results of a Reuters quarterly rand poll, the currency will depreciate to a quarterly average of 4.77 against the dollar in the fourth quarter of 1997 from 4.51 in the fourth quarter of this year.
Eight economists and currency analysts responded to the survey, predicting that the rand would weaken by between 2.5 percent and 7.8 percent from the fourth quarter.
Economists said a key indicator which would determine the level of the rand by the end of next year was the extent to which the country's balance of payments situation improved.

Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' recently cited the current account deficit as the central bank's prime concern after it deepened to 4.6 billion rand in the second quarter from 2.3 billion rand in the first quarter.
One currency analyst, who asked not to be identified, felt that there were few reasons to support a return of foreign capital inflows which were essential if the rand was to appreciate.
The analyst's view was shared by Standard Bank Economics Division, which noted that recent stability on the currency market had not been accompanied by any change in fundamentals.

Political and economic uncertainties such as crime, the country's future direction and concern about government's ability to implement its macro-economic strategy would continue to weigh on the currency, it said.

While the bank said that Finance Minister Trevor Manuel comments in Washington at the weekend committing the government to sound macroeconomic policies were to be applauded, the delivery of proposals set out in government's macro-economic strategy were needed to bolster confidence.
Until then, uncertainty would continue and the rand would remain vulnerable to short-term capital flows, it said.

The analyst also said that with initial expectations of a spike in inflation not being realised after the rand's collapse earlier this year and with the country's low level of reserves, he expected the rand to weaken in line with an inflation differential of about six percent.

"Assuming we don't have any major political catastrophe between now and (the end of 1997), the Reserve Bank is going to want to see the rand depreciate against the inflation differential of our major trading partners," he said.
Sandra Gordon, an economist analyst at Syfrets Managed Assets, was optimistic that the balance of payments situation would improve over the coming year.
"We are anticipating that a narrowing of the current account deficit over the next 18 months coupled with some kind of inflows...will provide support for the rand," Gordon said.
She said inflows could stem from government's planned 2.5 billion rand offshore borrowings this year as well as privatisation proceeds.

Gordon noted, however, an important factor which counted against the rand was expectations of lower growth in 1997. Economists generally expect GDP growth of about 2.6 percent next year after anticipated growth of three percent this year.
Kau Msimango, chief economist at iron and steel producer Iscor, said that with the recent stability in the South African economy, the rand was expected to return to its purchasing power parity (PPP).

"In the past the rand has deviated from its PPP for something like two years, but we think that with more stability in the South African economy...the rand is likely to revert back to its PPP much sooner because non-resident foreign exchange controls have been removed," Msimango said.
He also noted that real South African interest remained high in comparison with the country's major trading partners.
The rand, which fell to a record low of 4.59 to the dollar on August 19, has traded in a steady 4.48 to 4.52 range over the last four weeks, breaking above the 4.52 level late last week.
At close of trade on Monday it was trading at 4.5300/5350 against the dollar.
